searchText: I wrote my thoughts down here: https://unclebill.blog/posts/bid-feed (shameless blogpost plug) and also opened a PR with an alternative solution. Thank you, I really appreciate you gave it that much thought! > It converts the gossip bid path to a fallback. The BN uses gossiped bids only if the supplied bid fails. A higher value gossip bid cannot win. This is a net negative for the open builder market. I don't think this is entirely the case since the VC also considers gossip bids through its SSE subscription to `execution_payload_bid` right? I'm not sure if the `best_execution_payload_bid` event is truly necessary since the VC should already have access to gossip bids + p2p bids and therefore should already know the `best_execution_payload_bid` emitted. In terms of the problems identified with the current approach, how do you think about your solution vs solution A) described above? I personally think they are pretty similar both in terms of complexity and problems fixed. A) seems simpler from the VC point of view. ah yeah I think you're right about gossip bids via `execution_payload_bid` Without `best_execution_payload_bid`, the VC knows the highest bid, but not the best validated bid. The VC can't do any consensus checks e.g. the parent the BN intends to build on. w/ my solution i think one positive is that bid validation happens before block production. Additionally this allows VCs to implement bid streaming mechanisms which I think block builders would probably be interested in. > the parent the BN intends to build on Would that be the result of get_proposer_head? And could that not change in between the SSE event and produceBlock call? > bid streaming I think that would work with solution A) as well. Honestly I think A) is the simpler way to fix the issues. The VC requests bids on all branches, and then just submits a list to the beacon node that performs validation and includes the first bid it deems valid. With a fallback to its own pool + local payload if none of them work out. yeah tbh I dont care much about how this endpoint looks, the main issue for me is: > first bid it deems valid I think that's a net negative to an open builder market. the supplied bid(s) should compete with bids in the pool and local payload, not treat them as a fallback. esp relevant in the case when a gossip bid arrives but VC hasnt seen it yet as long as we treat the bids equally at block production time, i am okay with either option <@586161934425128960> also brought this point up with me earlier. We can specify the supplied bid(s) must compete with other bids the beacon node has seen, I'm ok with that bookmarked neat blog page

excerpts.author: serenita_io
excerpts.content:
Thank you, I really appreciate you gave it that much thought!

> It converts the gossip bid path to a fallback. The BN uses gossiped bids only if the supplied bid fails. A higher value gossip bid cannot win. This is a net negative for the open builder market.

I don't think this is entirely the case since the VC also considers gossip bids through its SSE subscription to `execution_payload_bid` right?

I'm not sure if the `best_execution_payload_bid` event is truly necessary since the VC should already have access to gossip bids + p2p bids and therefore should already know the `best_execution_payload_bid` emitted.

In terms of the problems identified with the current approach, how do you think about your solution vs solution A) described above? I personally think they are pretty similar both in terms of complexity and problems fixed. A) seems simpler from the VC point of view.

excerpts.author: 0xunclebill
excerpts.content:
ah yeah I think you're right about gossip bids via `execution_payload_bid`

Without `best_execution_payload_bid`, the VC knows the highest bid, but not the best validated bid. The VC can't  do any consensus checks e.g. the parent the BN intends to build on.

w/ my solution i think one positive is that bid validation happens before block production. Additionally this allows VCs to implement bid streaming mechanisms which I think block builders would probably be interested in.

excerpts.author: serenita_io
excerpts.content:
> the parent the BN intends to build on

Would that be the result of get_proposer_head? And could that not change in between the SSE event and produceBlock call?

> bid streaming

I think that would work with solution A) as well.

Honestly I think A) is the simpler way to fix the issues. The VC requests bids on all branches, and then just submits a list to the beacon node that performs validation and includes the first bid it deems valid. With a fallback to its own pool + local payload if none of them work out.

excerpts.author: 0xunclebill
excerpts.content:
yeah tbh I dont care much about how this endpoint looks, the main issue for me is:

> first bid it deems valid

I think that's a net negative to an open builder market. the supplied bid(s) should compete with bids in the pool and local payload, not treat them as a fallback. esp relevant in the case when a gossip bid arrives but VC hasnt seen it yet

excerpts.author: 0xunclebill
excerpts.content: as long as we treat the bids equally at block production time, i am okay with either option
